title: Suryakumar Yadav to Captain Mumbai in Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy
excerpt: Dropped from India's T20I side after leading them to World Cup glory, Suryakumar returns to lead Mumbai from November 14, with Dube, Sarfaraz and a returning Thakur in the squad.
body:
• Suryakumar Yadav will captain Mumbai in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy, the Mumbai Cricket Association announced on Monday, November 9, 2026.
  • The 16-member squad includes Shivam Dube, Sarfaraz Khan and Tushar Deshpande, and sees Shardul Thakur return from a finger injury.
  • Mumbai open against Hyderabad in Kolkata on November 14, in a group with Gujarat, Goa, Vidarbha, Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Uttarakhand.
  • It is Suryakumar's first competitive assignment since IPL 2026 — and his return after being dropped from India's T20I side and left out of Mumbai's Ranji Trophy squad.

Suryakumar Yadav is back in charge — of Mumbai, at least. The Mumbai Cricket Association announced on Monday that he will lead the side in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy (SMAT), India's domestic T20 tournament, which begins on November 14. Mumbai start against Hyderabad in Kolkata that day, Cricbuzz reported.

"It is always a matter of immense pride to represent Mumbai. We have a good mix of experienced players and exciting young talent, and I am confident that the team will come together, play with intensity and give its best in every match. Our aim is to go all the way and bring the trophy home."

— Suryakumar Yadav

A squad built on internationals

The 16-member squad pairs Suryakumar with T20I regular Shivam Dube, Sarfaraz Khan and Tushar Deshpande. Shardul Thakur returns after missing the first leg of the Ranji Trophy with an injury to his right middle finger, sustained in training before the tournament; he last played in the Duleep Trophy in the second half of August, according to ESPNcricinfo. Dube joins the side after not getting a game in India's five-match T20I series in New Zealand, which India won 3-2. The full squad: Suryakumar Yadav (capt), Angkrish Raghuvanshi (wk), Hardik Tamore (wk), Atharva Ankolekar, Shams Mulani, Divyansh Saxena, Maxwell Swaminathan, Suved Parkar, Musheer Khan, Sarfaraz Khan, Sairaj Patil, Shivam Dube, Shardul Thakur, Tushar Deshpande, Mohit Avasthi and Sylvester D'Souza. No vice-captain was named. One new face is Maxwell Swaminathan, a 27-year-old spin-bowling allrounder from the Mumbai T20 League.

Why this appointment matters

The context is what makes a domestic captaincy announcement news. Suryakumar led India to the T20 World Cup title at home in March, but after the IPL the selectors dropped him from the T20I side and named Shreyas Iyer captain, ESPNcricinfo reported; he had scored 270 runs in 13 innings in an IPL season in which Mumbai Indians finished ninth. He then missed out on Mumbai's Ranji Trophy squad altogether, while playing the Mumbai T20 league and club cricket. Mumbai have split their captaincy this season — Siddhesh Lad leads the Ranji side, which opened with four consecutive wins, and Lad has not been picked in the T20 squad. Mumbai will also be without Yashasvi Jaiswal, who is in New Zealand, and allrounders Suryansh Shedge and Tanush Kotian, who are in the squad for the 50-over Rising Stars Asia Cup in Doha from November 19.

What's next

Mumbai are pooled in Group D with Hyderabad, Gujarat, Goa, Vidarbha, Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Uttarakhand. The campaign opens on November 14 in Kolkata — the first competitive cricket for Suryakumar since the IPL, and the start of the run of form he will need if an India recall is to follow.
